Becoming an NSU Student
Important Update: Court Action on Duration of Status (D/S) Rule:
On Monday, September 14, 2026, a federal judge in the U.S. District Court for the
District of Massachusetts (Presidents' Alliance et al. v. DHS) has issued an injunction,
temporarily blocking DHS from implementing this rule for F and J visa holders. As
a result, the rule ending D/S will NOT take effect on September 15th as originally scheduled, and the current D/S framework
remains in place for now.
What this means is that:
You and your dependents may continue to be admitted and to remain in the U.S. for
Duration of Status, as long as you continue to comply with the terms of your program.
You do not currently need to apply for an Extension of Stay under the fixed-admission-period
system the new rule would have created
If you are an F-1 student, you are not subject to the rule's new limits on changing
your educational objective, transferring institutions, or pursuing additional programs
of study – these restrictions also do not go into effect while the preliminary injunction
is in place.
No action is required on your part at this time.
Please note that this is a preliminary court order, not a final resolution. The administration
may appeal, and the underlying litigation is ongoing. The rule may still take effect
later, depending on how the case proceeds. We will continue to monitor developments
closely and update you as soon as anything changes.
On July 17, 2026, DHS published a final rule establishing a fixed time period of admission and an extension of stay
procedure for F nonimmigrant academic students and J exchange visitors. This rule
is effective on September 15, 2026, and will impact several aspects of the F-visa
and J-visa program regulations. For detailed information regarding the DHS Final Rule,
we encourage you to visit Study in the States, the official online resource managed
by the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and the Student and Exchange Visitor
Program (SEVP) by clicking HERE. Accordingly, updates to our website content are in progress.
Nova Southeastern University's programs are administered through its 18 colleges and
schools at locations throughout Florida, across the nation, and at select international
sites.
U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) has approved NSU to accept and enroll
international students who will be attending classes at campuses in the South Florida
area (Dade, Broward, and Palm Beach counties), as well as regional campuses throughout
the state.
Start With The Admissions Process
We recommend contacting the NSU program that you are interested in applying to so
that you may obtain further information regarding their class locations in the tri-county
area. If you need assistance contacting NSU's program offices, please call 800-541-6682.
Undergraduate Admissions
Graduate and Professional Admissions
Once you have applied to your selected program, the Office of International Students
and Scholars will automatically contact you to get started with the I-20 process.
For more information on becoming an international student in the United States visit
the Education USA website.

Language Proficiency Information
Applicants whose native or official language is not English are required to demonstrate
English proficiency in order to be admitted into a degree program. Each program may
have additional requirements. Please check with the admissions department of your
program for its English proficiency requirements.
The following standardized tests currently satisfy the English language proficiency
requirements for the majority of NSU's colleges, schools and centers:
Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL)
International English Language Testing System (IELTS)
Pearson Test of English—Academic (PTE)
iTEP Academic (undergraduate admissions only)
GMAT
GRE
Scholastic Assessment Test (SAT)
American College Test (ACT)
Cambridge Certificate in Advanced English (CAE)
Duolingo English Test
Proof of English language competency can also be in the form of successful completion
of a degree at an approved U.S. institution of higher education or passing Level 9
at Talk International Language School.
Follow submission instructions of these test scores from the specific admission office
of the program you are applying to.
Credential Evaluations
Students applying for graduate or undergraduate transfer admission and who have completed
coursework outside the United States at a non-American institution must have their
foreign transcript go through a process called “Credential Evaluation.” This Credential
Evaluation is completed by organizations accredited by the National Association of
Credential Evaluation Services (NACES). Undergraduate, first-time-in-college applicants do not need to submit a credential
evaluation of their secondary school transcripts.
This Credential Evaluation is conducted by organizations that are accredited by the
National Association of Credential Evaluation Services (NACES). A list of these organizations
can be found at www.naces.org. The evaluation will determine if the student’s foreign degree is equivalent to the
degree that the program of choice requires. The evaluation must list the degree equivalency
and include a GPA (grade point average) calculation as well as a course-by-course
credit evaluation.
The prospective student is responsible for requesting this Credential Evaluation and
for following specific instructions from the admission’s office at the college/school
of his/her choice. Please see each school/college’s admission requirement information
for more details.
Transferring to NSU
USCIS allows transfers between institutions approved by the Student and Exchange Visitor
Information System (SEVIS). To transfer in to NSU, your current Designated School
Official (DSO) must electronically transfer your SEVIS record. Submit a completed
Transfer Authorization Form along with your I-20 requirements to intl@nova.edu. This must be completed before you begin your studies at NSU.
Transfer Authorization Form
View I-20 Requirements
Transferring out of NSU? Submit a Request for Transfer Out, acceptance letter from your new institution, and
a completed Transfer Request Form (from your new institution) to intl@nova.edu.
Request for Transfer Out
Important: Ensure both you and your current DSO complete the form before submitting it.
